question.problem: Construct the vector field that has the stream function $ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y-x.$

current_example.problem: Construct the vector field that has the stream function $\psi(x,y) = e^{x} \cos{y}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
A function $\psi(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $\mathbf F= P\,\mathbf{i} + Q\,\mathbf{j}$ if the following equations hold:

$$
P = \dfrac{\partial \psi}{\partial y},\qquad Q = -\dfrac{\partial \psi}{\partial x}
$$

Computing the partial derivatives of the function $\psi(x,y),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\frac{∂ψ}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y) \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y, \\ Q & =-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x} \\  & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y) \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function $\psi(x,y) = e^{x} \cos{y}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y) & =P\,i+Q\,j \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,j.\end{aligned}
$$
